names.classification: INTERNAL | PREPARED FOR YOU | NOT FOR THE PERSON DESCRIBED

plain_words.rule: Nothing the user reads -- the PDF, replies, setup questions, the listing -- uses military, intelligence-trade or technical jargon. Their own quoted words are exempt.

concepts: Work the intelligence cycle: direction (setup and the meeting objective) -> collection -> processing (each fact gets a source, tag, grade and date; excluded topics are dropped) -> analysis -> the {deliverable} -> feedback (the debrief).

Collection is open sources found by targeted web search in rounds, each refined from the last (osint), the person's public social footprint, LinkedIn only as its public search results show it (never a browser session), and the user's own files and answers (a LinkedIn profile they save is one).
{profile} is human-source analysis from public evidence: each row is a cited observation and the caller's move. It never labels the person's character.
Keep what was read apart from what was inferred (the grade). Check the one assumption the Take rests on (Strongest case against). On deep runs, weigh competing explanations of what they want.

ask_user.rule: Ask the user only when a trigger below fires: at most 2 questions per run after setup, in one message, each skippable. Never ask what the record or the saved setup already answers. Answers are the user's own facts: tag Yours.

triggers.when: No meeting objective in the intake
triggers.ask: What do you want to walk out of this meeting with?

triggers.when: Two or more people match the name
triggers.ask: Which of these is the person you're meeting?

triggers.when: The intake says you already know them, and no notes came with it
triggers.ask: When did you last speak, and what did they tell you that isn't public?

triggers.when: You mention notes, a CRM record, a Slack or Google Chat thread, a saved LinkedIn PDF or a profile on them
triggers.ask: Can you paste it or give me the file? I'll mark it as yours, not public.

triggers.when: Who decides, the gate or the timing is still Not determined after collection
triggers.ask: Who else has a say in this, as far as you know?

room.rule: Every Not determined (a **Label:** line or a table cell) and every No read in the {profile} is a gap. The ledger's Still open row asks at most 4 of them in the room, highest value first (who decides and the gate before the {profile}), each as 'Label: question?' in at most 10 words, items separated by ' · '. Open, non-leading, one idea each; never filler.

rules.text: Ask only the questions with no saved answer in ~/.pcp/profile.yaml -- all of them the first time, all again with --recalibrate. Otherwise read it silently.
rules.test: A profile with Q1-Q8 answered and no Q9 -- the run asks Q9 only. A complete profile -- it asks nothing.

rules.text: A skipped answer takes the first (Recommended) option and is stored with defaulted:true; the masthead's Prepared for and Depth show the saved answers.
rules.test: Skip Q5 -- profile shows research.depth standard, defaulted true; the masthead reads "Depth standard".

rules.text: The improve loop may PROPOSE a profile change (one line, with the debrief evidence) but never applies one without a yes.
rules.test: Three debriefs with facts_used > 80% must produce a proposal, and the profile must be unchanged until answered.

rules.text: Files named in Q8 (or later with --context <path>) are read once; their paths and a summary of at most 150 words go in the profile under context. Facts taken from them are tagged Yours, never presented as public. Supported: .pdf .docx .md .txt .csv. Any other file gets one line naming the supported types, and the profile is left unchanged.
rules.test: Give a one-page file -- the profile holds its path and summary, and a fact from it prints with tag Yours. Give a .pptx -- one line names the supported types and profile.yaml's sha256 is unchanged.
rules.basis: Oct 9: a user with a business context profile can upload files

rows.text: Public sources found by targeted web search in rounds (osint), plus what the user gives: their files and answers (tag Yours), a LinkedIn profile they save among them (S2-7). LinkedIn itself only as its public search results show it; never a signed-in or automated browser. No paid data the user has not supplied; nothing collected in bulk.
rows.test: A run with no files and no answers holds only Direct, Search and LinkedIn facts, and its transcript requests no linkedin.com page.
rows.basis: original plugin v1; Sep 28: use what people already have

rows.text: Every claim carries url (or the file name, for Yours), retrieved_at, published (the source's own publication or event date; none when the source is undated), tag Direct|Search|LinkedIn|Yours, grade Measured|Derived|Inference|Not determined, and confidence C1 (primary, dated) | C2 (reputable secondary) | C3 (single weak source) | C4 (inferred).
rows.test: A claim missing any field is dropped by eval.py duf and counted as dropped.

rows.text: A claim that hits an exclusion is dropped BEFORE the writer sees it and counted in coverage.excluded; the ledger's Left out on purpose row names the topic, never the fact.
rows.test: Seed a claim tagged exclusion health -- it must not appear in any output file.
rows.basis: original plugin v1 + every rule carries a falsification test

rows.text: Coverage is a required output: families_attempted/families_total and hits per family. A run without coverage is not a run.
rows.test: Disable WebFetch -- coverage must show 0/N attempted and status LIMITED, never FULL.

rows.text: Status FULL requires >= 1 C1/C2 claim in >= research.full_threshold[depth] families; else LIMITED, stamped in the masthead.
rows.test: Remove all C1/C2 claims from one family below threshold -- status flips to LIMITED.

rows.text: Run the counter-evidence family last: search for what would contradict the strategic read.
rows.test: With depth standard or deep, coverage must show family F12 attempted.

rows.text: LinkedIn is read the way the rest of the record is: by targeted web search in rounds (osint; references/osint-search.md), from the result text the host's search tool returns. Never request a linkedin.com URL, sign in, or open or drive a browser session (osint.never). With social scope none, or when the user says not to, run no LinkedIn query: 'not read: scope none' or 'not read: you declined'. A LinkedIn result is used only once it passes the identity lock (osint.identity_lock); when none passes: 'not read: no matching profile'. Its facts are graded as osint.grading says: tag LinkedIn, C3, cited [linkedin.com, search result](the profile URL the result lists), dated 'seen <today>', and 'per their LinkedIn' in a sentence that rests on it alone. Optional (AID-62, under review): when the user gives the person's LinkedIn profile saved as a PDF or copied text, read it as their file (tag Yours, cited by the file name; 'read from your file'); the run never waits for one. Every run states LinkedIn's status, the same in two places, B4's last line and the Coverage row: '**LinkedIn:** read from search results' or 'read from your file', or '**LinkedIn:** not read: <reason>', the reason one of linkedin.reasons word for word; not read: no fact is tagged LinkedIn. An unread LinkedIn is stated in Coverage only, never as a Still open question (Oct 14).
rows.test: A run on a public executive requests no linkedin.com URL and calls no browser tool (its transcript shows search calls only, for LinkedIn); the profile's search result is a ledger row cited to linkedin.com/in, and B4 and Coverage read 'LinkedIn: read from search results'. The identity-lock example reads 'not read: no matching profile'. A brief that says 'read in your browser' fails C16 (fixtures linkedin_search.md, linkedin_browser.md, linkedin_declined.md, linkedin_missing.md, linkedin_declined_with_row.md).
rows.basis: Oct 14 Ben/Danny meeting, AID-63: replace the browser opt-in (b5f1b88: the user's signed-in browser, which LinkedIn's terms bar for automated tools) with multi-round targeted search, public search results only. OSINT review Oct 15: platform terms, identity lock, grading, the round plan. AID-62 (a saved profile PDF) stays optional until Daniel decides; before Oct 15 the run asked for it and waited (28a2350).

rows.text: Source quality: prefer the primary source (the organisation, filings, the person's own words). Never cite a source_quality.exclude domain (people-search and unreachable sites); a source_quality.weak domain is at most C3 and never the only support for a fact on page 1. Cite a fact only where the ledger row says it: hypotheticals (Reverses if, Stop if) carry no citation. Before render, check every link: dead links are replaced or the fact is dropped; blocked links (the site refuses bots) are kept.
rows.test: A brief citing mexc.com as C2 fails C18; a Reverses if line citing the intake row fails C17; the link check reports blocked separately from dead.
rows.basis: Live test runs Oct 13 (R1 weak sources, R2 citations on hypotheticals)

rows.text: Research runs as the search rounds (osint), in order, each one the depth enables: round 1 (the identity lock, its LinkedIn query among them) before anything else, round 5 last. Write each round's queries down (coverage.rounds) before sending them, refined from what the round before confirmed or left open.
rows.test: The run's first searches are round 1's, the LinkedIn query through the domain filter where the tool has one; a run whose LinkedIn query comes last, or types site: into a tool that ignores it, fails (Oct 15 consumer run R10).
rows.basis: Oct 15 consumer run (c0c966d): 11 searches, the LinkedIn query last and typed as site:, which Claude's WebSearch ignores, so a public profile read as 'no matching profile'.

rows.text: Read each of the six dimensions only from observation_ids in claims.jsonl; a band with fewer observations than its tier minimum is reported as 'no read' -- never guessed from role.
rows.test: A target with only role-archetype claims must render every dimension as tier low and the script must contain no influence sequence.

rows.text: B6's evidence tier is the highest tier at least three of the six dimensions reach (a no read counts as low). It gates page 3: low -> no Read the room (P5); high AND authority_level high -> Influence (P6). Otherwise P6 is left out.
rows.test: Delete one corroborating claim -- the tier must drop and P6 must disappear on re-run.

rows.text: Every Your move in B6 is a rubric meaning in pcp.yaml, word for word, or No read; no band phrase is written in prose.
rows.test: Grep B6 for a move not in rubric.*.meaning -- the run is rewritten.

rows.text: Depth deep adds what they may want: <= 3 hypotheses about what the person wants from this meeting, each with the claim that would disprove it.
rows.test: Depth standard -- no hypotheses table in B8; depth deep -- the table, with a disproving claim [n] per hypothesis.

outputs.name: <out>/<date>-<slug>-intelligence-brief.pdf
outputs.note: ONE 3-page PDF via format/talyx_pdf.py --style brief --brief-pages 2 --max-pages 3; the script on page 3

rows.text: Every fact in B1-B9 and the script cites a ledger number [n]; the ledger (B10) lists only cited facts, numbered in order of first use. A fact with no citation is a defect, not a style choice.
rows.test: eval.py duf reports unbound or dangling > 0 -- the run must rewrite before render.

rows.text: Every sentence passes the swap test against caller.offer_one_line and the target: if another target's name would leave it true, delete it.
rows.test: A brief with a sentence containing no claim id and no target-specific noun fails checks.swap.
rows.basis: original plugin check 1, tightened to sentence

rows.text: Where the host can run scripts and a browser engine (Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT agent or work mode), render ONLY through format/talyx_pdf.py --style brief --brief-pages 2 --max-pages 3, never Markdown or HTML as the deliverable. The PDF is exactly 3 pages: the brief fills pages 1-2 (a short brief puts the evidence ledger on page 2 -- never filler) and the script is page 3. Check it with eval.py pdf. Where render is impossible, follow S4-10.
rows.test: On a script-capable host the output directory contains exactly one .pdf and no .md/.html after a run; eval.py pdf on it exits 0 (3 pages, the script on page 3 only, the ledger on page 2).
rows.basis: design choice, PDF first; AID-8: meeting script on page 3; Daniel Oct 13: PDF where scripts run

rows.text: Fact density (the ratchet's metric, decision-useful facts per page, never drops). Standard depth aims at 18 or more distinct cited facts across the 3 pages, at least 6 per page. Spend words on facts, not framing: a line that can carry a new cited fact carries one; cut uncited connective sentences; each B2 question, B3 bullet, B5 row, B8 bullet and P3 answer rests on a different [n] where the evidence allows. Before writing Not determined for Role since, Path, The organization or Decision maker, run one targeted search of the primary source (official bio, annual report or proxy statement, newsroom); for a public company these are almost always public. The ledger's What it says stays under 8 words so each row is one line. Each No read or Not determined is a gap on the page, so evidence that fills one frees space for a fact: search two long-form interviews or earnings-call remarks for the six reads before writing No read. Keep each Still open question under 10 words. Before rendering, run eval.py duf: below 6.0 per page, replace a repeated [n], an uncited line or a filled-in-able gap with a new cited fact from the claims, then re-check fit; if the brief overflows, cut words, not facts.
rows.test: eval.py ratchet: every frozen target's duf_pp meets its floor at 10 pt and 3 pages.
rows.basis: Daniel, Oct 14: floors never drop; recover density by wording, budgets and fact selection

rows.text: In-chat fallback. Render is impossible when the host has no shell or code tool, python3 is missing, or talyx_pdf.py exits for want of a browser engine (after one try of --setup where installs are allowed). Then deliver the full brief in the chat, never a summary: first line exactly 'Intelligence Brief (in chat: this app cannot make the PDF, so the same 3 pages follow as text)'; then the masthead lines; then the line '--- Page 1 ---' and B1-B6; '--- Page 2 ---' and B7-B10 with the same 5-column ledger (each row starts '| [n] |', the source a link or 'your request' / 'your saved setup') and its Coverage / Still open / Left out on purpose / Run rows; '--- Page 3 ---' and '# Meeting script' with P1-P9. Same blocks, order, titles, word budgets, citations [n], grades and plain-words rules as the PDF. Build the ledger from your claim list before writing the blocks, number facts in order of first use, and cite only those numbers; drop a row nobody cites. Never cite a source_quality.exclude domain. Action and Avoid in B1 each cite a fact. Every ledger row has a grade (Measured, Derived, Inference) and the source's own date 'Mon D, YYYY' ('seen Mon D, YYYY' only for an undated source). The LinkedIn line is a plain line after B4's bullets, never a bullet. Still open items are '<the exact label as printed>: <What/Who/How/When/Which/Where/If ...?>' joined by ' · ', at most 4, highest value first, each label a Not determined or No read above. Thin or no evidence never changes the shape: keep every block title and fill it with Not determined or No read; the top 4 gaps get a 'Label: question?' in Still open (S4-7). If a code tool exists, run eval.py checks on it; otherwise, before sending, check yourself, one line at a time, against these worked examples: (1) the first line is the label itself, nothing before it; (2) count B1's words: at most 60, e.g. '**Take.** Jane Doe has led Alder Grey since 2021 [1] and buys patience [3]. **Evidence:** her 2021 start [1] and her letter's 'we buy patience' [3]. **Action:** open on her letter [3]. **Avoid:** a fee-led pitch [4].' -- Evidence names the facts in words, never bare numbers; (3) P9 is one line of at most 25 words, e.g. '**Next step:** send the one-page example by Oct 17.', and nothing follows it but the Checks line -- no note, caveat or offer; (4) a hypothetical or a thing to learn carries no [n] unless the cited row says it, e.g. '**Reverses if:** she names a tooling owner.', '**Stop if:** they say tooling is settled.' and '**Capture:** who owns AI choices.'; (5) each Still open item is 'Label: question?' starting What, Who, How, When, Which, Where or If, never Does, Is, Can or Do, e.g. 'Decision maker: Who signs off?'; at most 4, each on a gap above; (6) Recent wins carries a date and a citation, e.g. '**Recent wins:** Jul 30, 2026: Azure passed $100 billion [3].', or the line is left out; (7) every sentence in B1 and B3-B8 carries a [n] or names the person or organization, e.g. 'Outside prep may look redundant to Microsoft [4].', never a bare 'Outside prep may look redundant.'; (8) block titles exactly as listed and in order, with no numbers ('## Take', '## Questions that close gaps'); only the script's sections are numbered; (9) the deliverable is only ever the Intelligence Brief, never a meeting brief, call brief, dossier or one-pager, even for the sample you bring; (10) a ledger date that is today's date is the day you read the source: write 'seen Oct 14, 2026' unless the source itself is dated today; rows from your request or your saved setup are always 'seen <today>'; (11) count every block against its budget, B9 included (at most 120 words); (12) no Left out on purpose topic appears anywhere, not even as a source name (no donations, no FEC filings); (13) every [n] in the ledger and every ledger row cited, no banned word; (14) each ledger row's What it says repeats the key words of the sentence that cites it, e.g. 'called for an AI emergency brake [3]' cites '| [3] | Called for an AI emergency brake |', not '| [3] | Oct 10 post: contain the model |'. End with 'Checks: self-reviewed, not run as code'.
rows.test: Run with no Bash tool: the reply holds the label, the three page markers, every B1-B10 and P1-P9 title in order, a ledger row per cited [n], and no plain_words.banned word; eval.py chat on the saved reply exits 0.
rows.basis: Daniel, Oct 13: plain chat in ChatGPT or Claude falls back to the full brief in chat

rows.text: If the tightest density rung still overflows 3 pages, the run FAILS with the section word counts; it never truncates or spills. An overflow is fixed only by cutting words in the sections the renderer names; never change --columns, --brief-pages or --max-pages, never drop or move a block (Oct 14: the R9 run stacked the schema's pairs to fit).
rows.test: Feed a 900-word section -- the engine must exit non-zero naming the section.

rows.text: The masthead's meta line carries meeting, prepared for, depth, sources, status and date; the ledger's Run row carries the run details; the footer carries only the {deliverable}, the person and the page numbers. The identity line is organization | role, since year | city: the city only when a source confirms it; anything unconfirmed or unknown is left out, never printed as '(not confirmed)', 'not published' or 'Not determined'.
rows.test: Extract page 1 text -- the meta line has all six fields; no page footer holds a metric.
rows.basis: Oct 7: run details under the sources

rows.text: A block or line prints only as its Prints when says: a line PCP cannot fill from evidence is left out, or reads Not determined where its row says so. Never filler.
rows.test: No recent wins found -- the Recent wins line is absent, not blank or padded.
rows.basis: Oct 9: if we can't produce it, parameterize it so it's conditional

rows.text: Every Not determined -- a **Label:** line or a table cell -- and every No read in B6 is a gap; the ledger's Still open row asks at most 4 of them, highest value first, as 'Label: question?', as references/socratic-questions.md says.
rows.test: Write five Still open questions, or one whose label is no gap above, or none while gaps exist -- eval.py checks fails C12 (fixtures control_broken.md, gaps_table.md).
rows.basis: Oct 9: Socratic questioning reference for things it can't find

rows.text: Plain words: nothing printed uses a plain_words.banned term or an internal code; the person's own quoted words are exempt.
rows.test: Put SOCMINT in B3 -- eval.py checks fails C11.
rows.basis: Oct 9: don't use mil/intel/tech words in actual outputs

rows.text: Experience (Q9) shapes page 3 only: new -> P1, P3 and P4 each end with a **Why:** line of at most 12 words; top -> the Hook and each objection's answer are at most 15 words; experienced -> neither.
rows.test: Set Q9 new -- P1, P3 and P4 each carry a Why line; set experienced -- none does. eval.py checks --experience <Q9> fails C15 otherwise (fixtures exp_new.md passes as new, exp_experienced_with_why.md fails as experienced).

rows.test: Lower a family weight so a target's duf_pp drops -- ratchet must exit non-zero and name the target.

osint.rule: Search in rounds, each refined from the last: what a round confirms or leaves open writes the next round's queries, and each query is written down (coverage.rounds) before it is sent. A round runs the source types enabled at the run's depth and is skipped when all of its types are off. Stop when every block's facts are cited, or are Not determined after their planned queries.
osint.operators: Where the search tool takes a domain filter (Claude's WebSearch: allowed_domains), put a site: domain there, not in the query text: that tool ignores site: typed in a query (Oct 15 runs: no LinkedIn result at all; with allowed_domains [linkedin.com], the profile's headline). Elsewhere write site: in the query. Use the operators the host's search honours: quotes and site: almost always; intitle:, inurl: and filetype: often; a date window through the tool's recency setting or after:. When the results show an operator was ignored, log the round as attempted with that operator ignored, rerun once with plain quoted terms, and filter dates and file types yourself from the URLs and snippets. An ignored operator leaves a gap; it never shows that nothing exists.
osint.never: Use only the result text the host's search tool returns for linkedin.com: never request a linkedin.com URL (profiles, posts or Pulse articles; an article republished elsewhere is opened there), never sign in anywhere, never open or drive a browser session (no computer use, no browser extension), and quote snippets minimally. The search provider's terms govern the query. Collect on the professional role only: the exclusions apply to every round, and a result that touches them by accident stays out of the brief.
osint.identity_lock: A LinkedIn result is a lead, not an identity. Use it only when (a) its headline or current role names the person and gives the organisation as their current position (not past experience or a post), and one other detail agrees with the organisation as found elsewhere (its city or region, or its web domain); or (b) a second independent source (the organisation's own site, a filing, a news article) ties that profile or that exact role to the person. A generic title (Owner, President, Founder) counts only with the organisation. A detail that contradicts (another city, another firm) rejects it. A profile URL seen only as a link on another page, with no result of its own, is a lead for the domain-filtered search, not a second profile. Two or more profiles pass: use none. Never pick by guess.
osint.example: Intake 'Mark Brown, Precision Metal Fab'. The firm's own site says Odessa, TX; the only LinkedIn result reads 'Mark Brown - Owner - Precision Metal Fab | Greater Cleveland'. The location contradicts, so nothing from it is used: '**LinkedIn:** not read: no matching profile'.
grading: Open the page behind a result before citing it and grade the page (C1 primary and dated, C2 reputable secondary); LinkedIn is the one source cited from its search result. A page that refuses the fetch (a bot wall, 401 or 403) keeps its fact at C3, logged 'not opened': a gap, not a finding that the fact is false. A page that is gone (404 or 410) is dead: cite another source or drop the fact (S2-8).

A LinkedIn result: tag LinkedIn, Measured for what the result shows (text across an ellipsis is not quoted as one), C3, the source written [linkedin.com, search result](the profile URL the result lists), the date 'seen <today>'. A fact resting on it alone says so in the sentence ('per their LinkedIn'); a role seen only there never prints as confirmed current.

Items with one origin (a press release, a wire story, the person's own bio: shown by attribution, a link or near-identical wording) count as one source, graded by that origin; a speaker bio, a company bio and their LinkedIn are one self-reported source. Corroboration needs a second item with a different origin.

rounds.name: identity lock
rounds.goal: one person, one current role, one profile, or a stop
queries: site:linkedin.com/in "{name}" "{org}" (the domain filter linkedin.com, where the tool has one)
"{name}" {title} -"{org}" (namesakes: the same name at another firm or city)
rounds.next: Two or more people could be the one you're meeting: stop and ask (S1-2). The organisation's own site and one other source tie the person to it: identity locked. Nothing ties them: continue on the organisation and say so in Coverage.

rounds.name: role and history
rounds.goal: dated moves, boards, how they got here
queries: "{name}" (intitle:bio OR inurl:bio OR inurl:leadership OR inurl:speakers OR inurl:team)
"{name}" appointed OR joined OR named OR promoted "{org}"
rounds.next: Each prior firm and board found here becomes a term in rounds 3 and 4.

rounds.name: last 90 days
rounds.goal: what changed for them and the organisation in the last 90 days
queries: "{name}" OR "{org}" announces OR appointed OR launches after:{date_90_days_ago}
"{org}" results OR funding OR acquisition OR partnership after:{date_90_days_ago}
rounds.next: A dated event here is the opener's hook and B3's Recent wins line.

rounds.name: their own words
rounds.goal: quotes with a date and a link
queries: "{name}" interview OR podcast OR keynote OR panel
rounds.next: Their recurring words feed In their words and the {profile}.

rounds.name: gaps and counter-evidence
rounds.goal: only what is still Not determined, and what contradicts the read
queries: "{name}" OR "{org}" decides OR approves OR budget OR committee
"{org}" layoffs OR departure OR decline OR criticism (the exclusions still apply)
rounds.next: What is still open after this round becomes a Still open question in the room.

base: family matters outside the public professional record

eu: any claim older than 5 years that is not a current role

signals: interrupts or redirects in recorded panels

meaning.low: Let them set the pace; ask before you propose.
meaning.mid: Match their pace; propose once, then ask.
meaning.high: Lead with the outcome in one sentence; they decide fast and dislike preamble.

signals: titles and awards foregrounded in bios

meaning.mid: Acknowledge one specific achievement, then move on.
meaning.high: Open with respect for a specific, recent, public achievement; never one-up.

signals: length and density of their writing

meaning.low: Headline and one proof point; offer detail only if asked.
meaning.mid: Headline, two proof points, a source on request.
meaning.high: Bring the numbers and the sources; allow silence after a question.

signals: career moves into or out of stability
public positions on new or unproven things

meaning.low: Reduce risk first: references, reversibility, small first step.
meaning.mid: Pair the upside with the safeguard in the same sentence.
meaning.high: Lead with the upside and the speed; do not over-hedge.

meaning.low: Direct disagreement is fine; they separate idea from self.
meaning.mid: Frame challenges as questions about the situation, not the person.
meaning.high: Never correct them in the room; ask a question that lets them arrive at it.

signals: benchmarks and rankings in their language

meaning.low: Frame around their own goals, not peers.
meaning.mid: One peer reference is useful; more is noise.
meaning.high: Name what peers are doing; they will want to be ahead of it.

sections.title: Take
sections.content: One paragraph: **Take.** who they are and why this meeting matters to them now, in one sentence, every clause cited. **Evidence:** the one to three facts it rests on [n]. **Action:** the first move in the room, on the fact behind it [n]. **Avoid:** the one move that loses the meeting, on the fact that shows why [n] -- never a generic line. It adds no fact the blocks below don't cite.

sections.title: Questions that close gaps
sections.content: 5 numbered questions, each <= 20 words, on the fact it rests on [n]; under each, one indented bullet: **Decides:** what the answer settles for you. **Ask:** whom -- the person, or who else is in the room. Ordered by what they decide; the mix follows the meeting type (Q4).

sections.title: Who they are
sections.content: Bullets, label first: **Role:** title and since when [n] (required). **Path:** the prior roles that matter [n]. **The organization:** in its own words, plus one scale figure [n]. **What changed:** one to three dated items, newest first [n]. **Recent wins:** none to two dated, cited results [n]. Path, The organization and What changed read Not determined if not found; Recent wins is left out. From F1 F2 F3 F4 F9.

sections.title: In their words
sections.content: 2-3 bullets, label first: **Topic, where, when:** "their exact words" [n]. None found: one line of themes from their public presence [n]; nothing at all: Not determined. Then always one last line, not a bullet: **LinkedIn:** read from search results, **LinkedIn:** read from your file, or **LinkedIn:** not read: and the reason (S2-7). From F5 F6 F8 and LinkedIn.

sections.title: Signals and what to do with them
sections.content: A table: | Observable | What to do with it |, three rows in this order: their priority and the gap, in their words [n] -> why this meeting matters to them; where your offer connects (Q8) [n] -> the bridge: the outcome you offer, not the method; the trigger, why now [n] -> the urgency, never invented. From F3 F10 F11 and Q8.

sections.title: {profile}
sections.content: A table: | What the record shows | Your move |, six rows, one per rubric dimension, each starting with its label (Pace and control, How they take recognition, Appetite for detail, Appetite for risk, How they take disagreement, How they keep score) and a colon: the cited observation in at most 8 words [n] -> the rubric's move word for word. A dimension with no evidence is the bare label and No read (| Pace and control | No read |), never "none found". Then one line: **Evidence tier:** high, medium or low (it governs page 3). A cited observation and a move, never a verdict on their character.

sections.title: Who decides
sections.content: Bullets: **Decision maker:** who signs off [n]. **The gate:** what must be true, or who must agree, before a yes [n]. **Relationship holder:** who the relationship runs through [n]. Unknown: Not determined (a gap Still open may ask). From F1 F3 F9 F11.

sections.title: Strongest case against
sections.content: Up to 3 bullets: **Against:** the best evidence against your read [n]. **Reverses if:** what would flip it. None found: No counter-evidence found. Deep runs only, then `### What they may want from this meeting` and a table | Hypothesis and why it fits | Test: who answers, and what would disprove it |, up to 3 rows, each with the claim that would disprove it [n]. From F12; litigation stays off the page.

sections.title: Meeting angle
sections.content: One label per bullet (only The ask and its Fallback share one). `### This meeting` then bullets: **Frame:** what this meeting is, in their terms; not a pitch. **Lands:** [n]. **Repels:** [n]. **What to bring:** one thing of value [n]. **The ask:** specific and bounded, who and how long [n] · **Fallback:** the smaller ask. **Stop if:** the answer that means drop the ask. `### Meeting two` then **Meeting two:** the next conversation if this one lands, on a fact from this brief. **Meeting three:** where it goes after that. `### After the meeting` then **Capture:** what to record from the room that the public record couldn't give. From Q8 and B3-B8.

sections.title: Evidence ledger
sections.content: One line: {n} facts cited; status {FULL or LIMITED} at {n} of 12 source types. Each fact is measured unless its grade says otherwise. Dates are the sources' own; 'seen' marks the day an undated source was read. Then the table | # | What it says | Source | Grade | Date |, exactly one row per cited fact in order of first use (never grouped): [n] · the fact in about 8 words · [domain](url) (a file name for your own files) · Measured, Derived, Inference or Not determined · the source's own date, Mon D, YYYY, or Mon YYYY when the source gives only a month (claims.jsonl published); only for an undated source, the day it was read, marked 'seen Mon D, YYYY'. The tag (Direct, Search, LinkedIn, Yours) and confidence (C1-C4) stay in claims.jsonl, not on the page (Ben, Oct 13). Then a label grid (empty header row) with four rows: **Coverage** -- n of 12 source types, what was not found and why, and LinkedIn: read from search results, LinkedIn: read from your file, or LinkedIn: not read: and B4's reason. **Still open** -- at most 4 gaps, highest value first, each with the question that closes it in the room ('Label: question?', joined by ' · '). **Left out on purpose** -- the excluded topics, never the facts. **Run** -- date · depth · meeting type · prepared for · jurisdiction · status · decision-useful facts per page.

script.title: {script}
script.subtitle: Facts choose the moves; read the room, not the record

intro: one insight they did not have

blocks.title: Open
blocks.content: Bullets: **Hook:** two sentences, said aloud, on a cited fact [n] -- in italics. **Credibility:** who you are, in one line, 30 seconds [n]. **Insight:** one thing they didn't have [n]. **Rule:** how to hold the opening's rapport through the questions.

blocks.title: Question order
blocks.content: Bullets: **Story:** **Process:** **Gate:** **History:** **Commitment:** -- B2's questions word for word, in the order the room needs, on the beats for the meeting type.

blocks.title: Objections: name it, then answer
blocks.content: 3 bullets: **Their likely objection:** *say it before they do, then the answer, at most 30 words* [n].

blocks.title: Close
blocks.content: Bullets: **Restate:** ask what would make it an easy yes, then say it back in their words. **Real deadline:** a date that actually moves [n]. **The ask:** B9's ask · **Fallback:** B9's fallback. **Follow-up:** what you promise to send, and when.

blocks.title: Read the room (watch, do not assume)
blocks.content: Bullets: **Fast, wants the answer:** **Asks for terms and data:** **Talks about people:** **Big picture, ideas:** -- what you do, from B6.

blocks.title: Influence, one fact behind each
blocks.prints: evidence tier high and caller authority high; each principle only where a cited fact backs it
blocks.content: Bullets, only for principles a cited fact backs: **Authority:** **Reciprocity:** **Commitment:** **Social proof:** **Liking:** **Scarcity:** (real limits only; never invented urgency) [n].

blocks.title: If it stalls
blocks.content: 2-3 bullets: **The move:** what restarts the conversation, from a fact in this brief [n].

blocks.title: Guardrails
blocks.content: Bullets: **Rule:** what never to promise or claim, for the jurisdiction (Q7). **Never say:** the guardrails.never_say phrases and the domain's forbidden claims, quoted.

blocks.title: Next step
blocks.content: One line: **Next step:** the one action and its date.

checks.name: swap
checks.passes_when: no sentence in B1 or B3-B8 lacks both a [n] and a target-specific noun (headings, the tier line and Not determined lines aside)

checks.name: bound
checks.passes_when: unbound == 0, dangling == 0, and every [n] in the body is a B10 row | [n] | what it says | source | grade | date | (tag and confidence stay in claims.jsonl, Ben Oct 13)

checks.name: quotes
checks.passes_when: every quoted string in B4 has a [n]

checks.name: custom_q
checks.passes_when: >= 2 questions in B2 carry a [n]

checks.name: sections
checks.passes_when: B1-B10 and P1-P9 present in order (P5 and P6 may be left out per S3-2)

checks.name: budgets
checks.passes_when: no section exceeds its words by > 15%

checks.name: never_say
checks.passes_when: no never_say phrase appears outside P8

checks.name: outcome
checks.passes_when: B5 contains no method verbs from checks.method_verbs

checks.name: exclusions
checks.passes_when: no excluded topic keyword appears in the body

checks.name: pages
checks.passes_when: exactly 3 pages: the brief on pages 1-2 with the evidence ledger last on page 2, the script on page 3, page 3 of 3 in the footer, a link for every ledger row not tagged Yours; page 3's numbered sections run 1, 2, 3 ... with no gap when a section drops

checks.name: plain
checks.passes_when: no plain_words.banned term or internal code outside quoted words

checks.name: gaps
checks.passes_when: Still open holds at most 4 items, and at least one while B1-B9 show a gap (a Not determined **Label:** line or table cell, or a No read in B6); each item is 'Label: question?', the label a gap above, the question starting What, Who, How, When, Which, Where or If

checks.name: conditional
checks.passes_when: B8's hypotheses only when the meta line says Depth deep; P6 only when B6 says Evidence tier: high; P5 not at tier low; B3's Recent wins line only with a dated, cited result (never Not determined or blank)

checks.name: layout
checks.passes_when: the brief has exactly the 9 blocks B1-B9 before B10, and B10 is its last block: no other block and nothing after the ledger; B9 has one label per line (The ask with its Fallback excepted); nothing prints '(not confirmed)', and the identity line prints nothing unknown

checks.name: experience
checks.passes_when: new: P1, P3 and P4 each have a **Why:** line of at most 12 words; experienced and top: no Why line; top: the Hook and each objection's answer are at most 15 words

checks.name: linkedin
checks.passes_when: B4 has exactly one **LinkedIn:** line: read from search results, read from your file, or not read: one of linkedin.reasons (a brief run before a linkedin.retired reason's day may give it); Coverage states the same; read from search results: a ledger row cites the linkedin.com/in profile the result showed; read from your file: no ledger row cites a linkedin.com/in profile (the file is cited); not read: no ledger row is tagged LinkedIn and Still open asks nothing about LinkedIn

checks.name: cites
checks.cmd: eval.py checks --cites (eval.py cites brief.md --fetch reads the pages too)
checks.passes_when: every cited sentence shares content with the ledger claim it cites (2+ content words, 1 when the claim is 3 words or fewer) and every [n] is a ledger row; a hypothetical (Reverses if, Stop if) carries no citation unless the row says it

checks.name: quality
checks.passes_when: no ledger row cites a source_quality.exclude domain; a source_quality.weak domain is never C1 or C2; fewer than 3 ledger rows carry the run's own date unmarked (those are read dates: give the source's date, or 'seen' when it has none)

checks.name: render
checks.passes_when: every page: no ink within 0.12in of a page edge, no word outside the 0.3in side margins; no page ends more than 0.5in above its footer margin; the schema's pairs (B3|B4, B5|B6, B7|B8) print side by side (Oct 14: a thin run's page 3 ended 2in short); page 1: the logo is whole in the top-right masthead; no block runs across a page break: page 2 opens on Who decides (B7, as in the schema) and no table prints its header row on two pages

checks.name: colors
checks.passes_when: every printed character is Midnight #0F2744, black #000000 or white #FFFFFF (Ben, Oct 14: no gray, three colors, so the page reads when printed); the hairline #E8EAED is for rules only, never text

eval.definition: decision-useful fact = a ledger number [n] that is (a) cited in B1-B9 or P1-P9, (b) a B10 row with what it says, source, grade and date (tag and confidence in claims.jsonl), (c) target-specific (passes swap). duf_pp = count / pages.
